text:
incident-bot: PAGING: High queue backlog detected for service=runtime-inference-prod region=us-west-2. queue_length=12,345; avg_enqueue_latency=4.2s; autoscaler_desired=6 autoscaler_current=2. paging on-call: alex :rotating_light:
PagerDuty: PagerDuty incident PDR-83421 triggered for service runtime-inference-prod (Urgent)
alex: acked on PagerDuty. looking now. grabbing logs
sana: jumping in to help — on-call handover in 10m if you need me to take it
alex: thanks. top-level customers reporting 503s and elevated 5xx. route-level errors spiking on /v1/generate.
ops-bot: current incidents linked: PDR-83421 -> https://pagerduty.local/incidents/PDR-83421
mike: past 5m: scheduler shows repeated "FailedScheduling: 0/8 nodes available: insufficient nvidia.com/gpu" and CREATION_RATE of new pods < expected. autoscaler metrics show scale-up requests queued.
alex: can we temporarily increase pool capacity manually? what's blocking new nodes?
jess: cloud-side: hitting vCPU/GPU quota in us-west-2 for the project. I've requested quota bump but that takes ~15min. I can spin up a small set of dedicated instances if we allow preemptible/spot nodes; they should join within ~7-12m.
alex: do it. put them in the same ASG, taint tolerations match.
ops-bot: executing emergency scale command:
```
rctl pool scale --pool inference-prod-usw2 --replicas 12 --reason "emergency backlog" --mode emergency
```
ops-bot: command accepted, creating nodes (request id req-94fd)
mike: also seeing kube-controller-manager stuck on creating PVs for model-shards: error="Insufficient capacity in AZ a" — some pods pending for storage. we'll fall back to routing smaller model variants to reduce PV needs.
alex: initiating traffic routing fallback: prefer model-variant=small-memory; reduce concurrency to 1 per pod to avoid OOMs.
product-support: FYI egress: multiple paying customers hitting increased latency and 503s; support triage emailing affected accounts with temporary mitigations.
sana: while nodes spin up, switching routing policy to degrade gracefully. updating route config:
```
{
  "service": "runtime-inference-prod",
  "routing": {
    "primary": "rlextra-large",
    "fallback": "rlextra-small",
    "prefer_fallback_under_pct": 70
  }
}
```
mike: applied routing change. traffic to heavy models is down by ~65% now — enqueue rate dropping. queue_length: 12,345 -> 7,100 in 4m.
jess: cloud nodes provisioning: 4/8 up. GPU quota bump still pending but partial nodes created on new AZs.
alex: PagerDuty: acknowledged by alex, escalated to L2 (mike) and infra (jess). Marking incident as active.
Tim: I'm seeing autoscaler logs: autoscaler-controller tried to calculate desired replicas but the metric publisher had a 1m outage; desired_replicas stayed at 6 even though queue growth required 20. we lost 4x scaling signal due to metric pipeline lag.
alex: that's the root cause likely. autoscaler couldn't see queue metric in near-real-time and so didn't request scale fast enough.
ops-bot: manual pod restarts to free stuck schedules:
```
kubectl -n inference rollout restart deployment/worker-pool-a
```
ops-bot: restarted 6 pods across nodegroups
mike: new pods pending -> 3 get scheduled on the newly created nodes. queue_length -> 2,300. enqueue_latency -> 0.9s. error rate down 80%.
jess: all planned emergency nodes live. storage PVs still catching up, but routing fallback is keeping service stable.
alex: updating status to: Mitigating — partial capacity up, routing fallback active, backlog draining. Notifying PG and CS.
product-support: emailed affected customers with mitigation steps and ETA for full recovery.
sana: handoff: I'm taking primary on-call from alex in 8 minutes. alex, anything to call out for post-incident?
alex: handoff notes: root cause likely autoscaler metric pipeline lag + quota limits causing slow node provisioning. actions taken: emergency scale, routing fallback, pod restarts. Next: fix metric publisher reliability and add synthetic probe that validates autoscaler sees queue metric in <15s.
sana: ack takeover. I'll stay on for the next 40m and coordinate postmortem owner assignment.
PagerDuty: PDR-83421 acknowledged by alex, status: acknowledged -> in_progress
ops-bot: current timeline:
- 00:00 incident detected by queue alert
- 00:02 PagerDuty page fired
- 00:04 ack by alex
- 00:06 routing fallback applied
- 00:09 emergency nodes requested
- 00:18 nodes online and pods scheduled
- 00:22 backlog drained below critical threshold

mike: final checks: error budget for us-west-2 route used 18% today; we cut it down. 95th latency back to baseline 120ms.
jess: cloud tickets: quota bump approved but we should automate a safety buffer to avoid hitting hard limits. opening infra ticket INFRA-4019.
alex: I'll create a postmortem doc and link infra and autoscaler owners. owner: sana (postmortem lead), assignees: mike (runtime), tim (metrics), jess (infra).
sana: created postmortem draft: https://redwood.internal/pm/postmortems/PDR-83421-draft. adding timeline and logs.
ops-bot: closing actions (deferred): 1) tune autoscaler thresholds and add re-check for metric pipeline; 2) add quota guard that preemptively requests quota bump at 80% usage; 3) improve fallback routing tests.
alex: resolved: backlog cleared, services stable. will handoff to sana in 3m. great work everyone. :clap:
product-support: closing customer comms loop — customers acknowledged and grateful for quick mitigation.
sana: officially taking on-call. I'll follow up with postmortem and remediation tickets. leaving thread for async updates. :white_check_mark:
